Subject: Private VPC demarc & tenant egress proofing — request for deployment runbook

Hi Neha / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As part of our compliance review I need a concise deployment runbook and reference artifacts that show how Redwood will enforce control-plane / data-plane demarcation and tenant egress proofing for our on-prem footprint. Specifically we need:

- A single-page reference diagram we can include in our architecture binder showing control vs data plane boundaries, NVA/edge proxies, and egress relay points.
- A brief runbook (checklist style) that demonstrates the sequence of steps to validate egress proofing in staging and production.
- Evidence items we can attach to our security review (BGP/session snapshots, KMS flow diagram, sample audit log entries).

Target deadline: 2026-05-22 COB (we have an internal review on the 24th).

I've attached our network inventory (partial) to help reconcile address ranges. Also looped in Mateo + Jonas for ops/acceptance questions. Could we do a short sync (30m) on Thu or Fri to walk the artifacts?

Thanks,
Sara

On Mon, May 17, 2026 at 11:03 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. We'll put together a focused package that covers the items you listed.

Quick technical notes to seed the runbook and evidence checklist:

1) Control / data plane demarcation (acceptance checks)
   - Verify control-plane traffic limited to mgmt CIDR: 10.254.0.0/22 (staging) / 10.254.4.0/22 (prod). Confirm ACLs on edge proxies block tenant traffic to mgmt CIDR.
   - Confirm API control-plane endpoints are reachable only over the mgmt VPC interface; sample tcpdump and curl commands will be provided.

2) Tenant egress proofing (evidence)
   - Validate NAT/egress relay addresses: we will provide sample tcpdump + conntrack snapshots showing tenant traffic egressing via relay IPs (sanitized).
   - BGP proof: provide BGP table dump (filtered) and bgp session-state logs for the peering session with your border router.

3) KMS/key-flow
   - KMS calls are proxied via a service account in the mgmt plane; keys never transit tenant-side networks. Documentation will include a flow diagram and sample audit log lines (CloudKMS/HSM).

4) Acceptance artifacts (packaged)
   - diagram PNG, runbook markdown, kms checklist PDF, bgp_dump.txt (redacted), tcpdump_sample.pcap.txt (sanitized), audit_sample.log

Action items for runbook:
- Jonas: stitch in the exact BGP neighbor IPs and routing filters from Arcadia inventory.
- Mateo: produce KMS flow diagram + sanitized audit snippets.
- Neha: assemble the single-page binder and schedule the sync.

I'll attach the KMS checklist and a sample command list for validation. If Arcadia wants a signed evidence binder we can produce a stamped PDF as well.

—Kim
